steps.title: Recon: read the full psycopg2 + Spark JDBC connection lifecycle in this repo (dbManager.create_postgres_connection, SparkDAL._ensure_connection/_reconnect/execute_query/delete_query/delete_by_scope_batched/count_rows_by_scope/write_to_postgres, jobBase Spark conf, script.py call order) and record how many connections one run opens, when, and for how long
Confirm or refute the append+retry duplicate-row defect by reading script.py:493-604 and sparkDAL.write_to_postgres; state the concrete row-count consequence and which lanes are affected
Confirm or refute that SparkDAL._ensure_connection cannot detect a server-side drop (psycopg2 .closed semantics), and identify every call path that depends on it

Reconstruct the 2026-08-18 burst arithmetic: count concurrent workflow runs from the Glue API, multiply by measured per-run connection cost (task slots, not partitions), compare against the observed 967/968 ceiling, and name every unknown term
Establish what the parser contributes to connection pressure vs what the RDS Proxy, Glue MaxConcurrentRuns and the ICM batch fan-out contribute; attribute the ceiling breach
Assess the Spark 3.3.0 savePartition rollback-leak claim (JdbcUtils.scala:748) against the installed Spark version and determine whether the leak is reachable from this repo's write path
Assess alert fidelity: trace how a handled psycopg2 recovery in delete_query becomes a Slack 'Controller Exception', and identify what in this repo controls that

Write the plan: candidate changes split repo-owned vs infrastructure-owned, each with expected effect, blast radius, and how it would be validated; plus open questions with the exact command or access needed
